validity.researcher_notes: SCOPE ESTABLISHED FIRST: this row is the Delta Lateral Project, a single FERC-certificated LATERAL off the Kern River mainline (the ~1,700 mi Wyoming->Utah->Nevada->California trunk is system row P0207, already swept elsewhere in this campaign) -- not the system itself. Existence: independently confirmed via (1) Kern River Gas Transmission Company's own project page and fact sheet PDF (both operator self-disclosure, one origin; live URLs now serve only a JS stub, so cited via Wayback captures which carry the full text) describing 'the Delta Lateral Project...an approximately 36-mile, 24-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline' from 'Kern River's mainline near Holden, Utah, to a delivery point near Delta, Utah,' FERC Docket Nos. PF20-4 (pre-filing) and CP21-197 (certificate, granted May 19, 2022), built spring-fall 2023, in-service spring 2024; and (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, which tracks this exact project (docket PF20-4 then CP21-197) across 8 releases from Jan 2021 (Pre-applied) through Aug 2026 (Completed), agreeing on operator, state, docket, length (35 mi), diameter (24 in), capacity (140 MMcf/d), cost ($93.1M) and in-service date (2024-04). Two independent origins (operator self-disclosure + federal EIA compilation), both naming the project explicitly -- not a GEM-only entity. Classification: correctly classified as an interstate natural gas transmission lateral (EIA labels it 'Interstate'/'Lateral', FERC-regulated under the NGA) -- not oil, not gathering/feeder. Duplicate check against all 41 other rows in this batch's roster: none describes Holden-to-Delta, Utah termini or this docket; the row is not a re-listing of the Kern River mainline (P0207, out of this batch) or of any other roster pipeline. Real, correctly classified, not a duplicate.
